quote: India’s real GDP is expected to grow by 9 per cent (+/- 0.25) in 2011-12.
quote_2: Hence the point expectation for India’s growth is 9 per cent.
notes: Chapter 1 'State of the Economy and Prospects', para 1.69-1.70. Point forecast 9% with stated +/-0.25 band. 2004-05 base; headline 'real GDP' then meant GDP at factor cost at constant prices. In the PDF '2011-' ends a line and '12' starts the next (text layer gives '2011- 12').

quote: a forecast of the growth rate of real GDP for 2012-13 to be 7.6 (+/-0.25) per cent.
notes: Chapter 1 para 1.82. Point forecast with +/-0.25 band. 2004-05 base, GDP at factor cost. Survey released in March (Budget on 16 Mar 2012). '2012-' ends a line in the PDF (text layer gives '2012- 13'). Same para also gives 8.6% for 2013-14 (preliminary).

quote: the overall economy is expected to grow in the range of 6.1 to 6.7 per cent in 2013-14.
notes: Chapter 1 para 1.76. 2004-05 base, GDP at factor cost. Sentence begins '...where all the three major sectors of the economy perform better in 2013-14 as compared to 2012-13,'.

quote: the GDP at factor cost at constant prices expected to grow in the range of 5.4 – 5.9 per cent in 2014-15.
notes: Election year: no survey in Feb 2014 (interim budget). The July 2014 survey is titled 'Economic Survey 2013-14' (not 2014-15) on the document itself. Chapter 1 para 1.64; explicitly GDP at factor cost, constant (2004-05) prices. Dash between 5.4 and 5.9 is an en dash; the margin box on the same page says 'grow in the range of 5.4-5.9 per cent in 2014-15'. A naive full-page text dump interleaves the margin box with this sentence; the quote is the main-column text. Para 1.65 adds growth is expected to be 'more on the lower side of the range'.

quote: Using the new estimate for 2014-15 as the base, this implies growth at market prices of 8.1-8.5 percent in 2015-16.
notes: Volume I chapter 1 'Economic Outlook, Prospects, and Policy Challenges'. First survey on the new 2011-12 base series; forecast is real GDP at market prices. '8.1-' ends a line in the PDF (text layer gives '8.1- 8.5'). A footnote marker '4' follows 'last year' in the preceding sentence.

quote: we expect real GDP growth to be in the 7 to 7¾ per cent range, with downside risks
quote_text_layer: we expect real GDP growth to be in the 7 to 73/4 per cent range, with downside risks
quote_2: be in the range of 7.0 to 7.75 per cent in the coming year.
notes: Volume I chapter 1 para 1.50. The ¾ is typeset as small '3/4' glyphs, so the PDF text layer reads '73/4'. Volume II chapter 1 para 1.66 repeats it as 'GDP growth that could be in the range of 7.0 to 7.75 per cent in the coming year' (quote_2).

quote: we expect real GDP growth to be in the 6¾ to 7½ percent range in FY2018.
notes: Volume I chapter 1 para 1.66 (FY2018 = 2017-18). Volume II (published Aug 2017, echap01_vol2.pdf p33, para 1.136) restated the 6.75-7.5 range but said the balance of risks had shifted to the downside, with outcomes near the upper end having much less weight.

quote: a pick-up in growth to between 7 and 7.5 percent in 2018-19 can be forecasted
notes: Volume I chapter 1 para 1.76 (Outlook for 2018-19). quote_2 is from the chapter's opening summary on pdf page 1 ('This should allow real GDP growth to reach 6¾ percent for the year as a whole, rising to 7-7½ percent in 2018-19').

quote: the economy is projected to grow at 7 per cent in 2019-20.
notes: Election year: no survey with the Feb 2019 interim budget; survey published July 2019. Quote is in Volume II chapter 1 'State of the Economy in 2018-19: A Macro View' (Volume I chapter 1 is about private investment and does not state the forecast). Sentence starts 'Given the macroeconomic situation and the structural reforms being undertaken by the government,'.

quote: India’s GDP growth is expected to grow in the range of 6.0 to 6.5 per cent in 2020-21.
notes: Volume II chapter 1 'State of the Economy', para 1.59 (right-hand column; a plain text dump interleaves the two columns). Volume I chapter 1 ('Wealth Creation') has no forecast. Real GDP implied (not stated as 'real' in the sentence).

quote: India’s real GDP is projected to record a growth of 11.0 percent in 2021-22 and nominal GDP by 15.4 per cent.
nominal_quote: India’s real GDP is projected to record a growth of 11.0 percent in 2021-22 and nominal GDP by 15.4 per cent.
notes: Volume II chapter 1 'State of the Economy 2020-21: A Macro View', para 1.61 (Outlook). Note the document prints '11.0 percent' (one word) but '15.4 per cent'. Followed by 'These conservative estimates reflect upside potential...'.

quote: India’s GDP is projected to grow in real terms by 8.0-8.5 per cent in 2022-23.
notes: Chapter 1 'State of the Economy', para 1.44 (Growth Outlook). Sentence begins 'Thus,'. Assumptions: no further debilitating pandemic disruption, normal monsoon, orderly liquidity withdrawal, oil at US$70-75/bbl.

quote: the survey projects a baseline GDP growth of 6.5 per cent in real terms in FY24.
quote_2: The actual outcome for real GDP growth will probably lie in the range of 6.0 per cent to 6.8 per cent
notes: Chapter 1 para 1.34. Baseline (point) 6.5% with a stated likely outcome range of 6.0-6.8% (quote_2, same para). Sentence begins 'Against this backdrop,'. No nominal projection found in chapter 1 or the preface.

quote: the Survey conservatively projects a real GDP growth of 6.5–7 per cent, with risks evenly balanced, cognizant of the fact that the market expectations are on the higher side.
notes: Chapter 1 'State of the Economy: Steady as She Goes'. Election year: no Economic Survey in Jan 2024 (interim budget 1 Feb 2024); this July 2024 survey is the relevant one. The dash in '6.5–7' is an en dash. The sentence does not name the year; context (Outlook section) is FY25. Sentence begins 'Considering these factors,'. In Jan 2024 the Finance Ministry instead issued 'The Indian Economy – A Review' (reported as saying FY25 real GDP growth 'will likely be closer to 7 per cent'); NOT verified here, because I could not find an official-site copy (only third-party copies), and it is not an Economic Survey.

quote: we expect that the growth in FY26 would be between 6.3 and 6.8 per cent.
notes: Chapter 1 'State of the Economy: Getting Back into the Fast Lane', para 1.72. The sentence says 'growth' without 'real GDP'; the chapter context is real GDP. Sentence begins 'On balance of these considerations,'. The sentence is split across pdf pages 32-33; the quoted part is entirely on page 33.

quote: the Economic Survey projects real GDP growth in FY27 in the range of 6.8 to 7.2 per cent.
notes: Chapter 1 'State of the Economy: Pushing the Growth Frontier', para 1.46. URL is the current-survey path; it will likely move to https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2026-27/economicsurvey/... when the next survey is published. Same para says medium-term potential growth is 'closer to 7 per cent'. No nominal projection found in chapter 1.
